title: Check: Reactions of Acids with Carbonates (2) (B)

questions.stem: Why do limestone buildings become damaged by acid rain?

options.text: Acid rain melts the stone at high temperatures
The calcium carbonate in limestone reacts with the acid, gradually dissolving it
Acid rain causes the stone to rust
Acid rain changes the colour of limestone but does not damage it

questions.explanation: Limestone is made of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), which reacts with acids in acid rain. The carbonate dissolves over time as it reacts to form soluble calcium salts, water, and CO₂. This gradually wears away the stone surface.
